_schema: world size (as a string) -> the measured peak for that world. A key exists only if a run at THAT world size reported it; extrapolating from another world is what gate_memory_measured refuses.
_caveat: Every peak here is RANK 0 (train.py's log line is is_main), so each is a LOWER bound on the worst rank -- per-rank DDP buckets differ. Safe to rule from at 25 GiB of headroom; NOT safe below about 10 GiB, where every rank has to report before the number means anything.
_why_not_nvidia_smi: nvidia-smi reads the caching allocator's reservation, not the high-water mark of live tensors. It returned 74.10 GiB at world=3 and 74.09 at world=7 -- the DDP bucket growth these measurements exist to find is invisible to it, because a larger bucket is served from cache the allocator never returns. Every fits/does-not-fit call in this repo before train.py:2604 (661e5ce) came from that number.

7.config: b32 accum1 d1024 L32 h8 ffn3072 seq4096 grad_ckpt compiled fp8 attn_res-Full

7_alt_b16a2.config: b16 accum2 -- same 917,504 tok/step as b32 accum1, half the activation set
7_alt_b16a2.role: control, not fallback. Its purpose was to prove the peak field tracks configuration at all -- the prediction that it must read materially lower was recorded in eff.w7_peak_memory_b32_fits before this arm ran. It is also the reserve: where 33 GiB comes from if seq or mix complexity grows.

_model.predicted_from: 493.6M params x 2 bytes x 3 copies (weights + Muon momentum + grads); agreement to 0.19 GiB is what makes this a model rather than a two-point fit
_model.note: Peak is LINEAR in batch. A first reading that grad_ckpt made activations sub-linear was wrong. Extrapolations from this line assume activation memory scales with seq the way it scales with batch, which is UNTESTED -- attention's quadratic term and the KDA recurrent state need not move together. On that assumption seq 8192 puts b32 at ~136 GiB (does not fit) and b16a2 at ~70 GiB (fits), making b32 the ceiling for this card at seq 4096.
